**Accuracy.** Response A adds "No action is required from the team." The release notes never say this, so it is an invented claim a manager might rely on. A also writes "35°C" where the source says only "35 degrees." Celsius is a plausible reading, but it is still an addition. Response B stays faithful to the source. Its slight generalisations, such as "time zone errors for New Zealand users" (the source says "some users"), don't mislead in any meaningful way.

**Coverage.** Both keep the key points: the three new features, the 35-degree threshold, the 15% battery figure, the fixes and accessibility. A keeps a few more specifics: the Settings path, the 15-minute sync interval, "all buttons." These are correct but not essential for a manager. B drops the off-the-page details reasonably and also notes who benefits from the pace chart change (colour-blind users).

**Concision.** A runs to roughly 140 words, which breaks the explicit under-120-word limit. B fits comfortably within it.

Overall, A has an unsupported added claim and exceeds the word limit. B is accurate, complete enough and within the limit.

Verdict: B
